Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 6) shows a small, opaque right hemithorax with dextroposition of the heart and mediastinum, consistent with right lung hypoplasia. Combined with the CT findings of an anomalous vein (Figures 4 and 5), these features are diagnostic for Scimitar syndrome, which is frequently associated with right upper lobe aplasia or hypoplasia.
